items.title: Swimming pool reopens in Mississauga after emergency repairs completed
items.summary: The swimming pool at Churchill Meadows Community Centre in Mississauga’s west end will reopen to regular programming this weekend after emergency repairs were completed, the city says. The indoor aquatic facility at the $51-million state-of-the-art community centre was closed to the public at the end of the summer after it “experienced an unexpected leak with the sprinkler system that required emergency repairs,” City of Mississauga officials said in an update to the community. The city said earlier this week the 25-metre, six-lane pool and therapeutic pool are now open once again. Drop-in swimming resumed this past Monday while regular registered programming is scheduled to resume this Saturday. Following the closure of the pool, aquatic programming was either cancelled or re-located to surrounding community centres. “We recognize that this caused inconvenience for users and residents and extra pressure on facilities and staff,” the city said in its update to the community this week. -ft. community centre, which also includes among many other amenities a triple gym, multipurpose room with a teaching kitchen and an active living studio, opened in late 2021. It’s part of a huge 57-acre complex on Ninth Line just north of Erin Centre Blvd. that also includes Mattamy Sports Park.

items.title: Everything you need to know about fall leaf collection in Mississauga
items.summary: With autumn leaves piling up on lawns, driveways and residential streets, Mississauga residents may be wondering when the city will be coming around to collect them. The City of Mississauga operates a seasonal vacuum leaf pickup program in selected neighbourhoods, but collection dates vary depending on where residents live. There are also some changes to the collection zones this year, making it important to check the schedule before raking leaves to the curb. Here is everything residents need to know about the 2026 fall leaf collection program. Which neighbourhoods are included in leaf collection? Not every Mississauga neighbourhood qualifies for the city’s vacuum leaf pickup service. The program is available on streets that are more than 35 years old and have a significant number of large, mature trees. The city divides eligible neighbourhoods into three colour-coded collection zones: yellow, blue and green. Each zone has two scheduled pickup periods during the fall. How can I find out which collection zone I live in?

items.title: $11M house with underground tunnel for sale in Mississauga
items.summary: An enormous home that’s become known as “Lorne Park’s Casa Loma” has hit the market in Mississauga. Today, Sam McDadi Real Estate Brokerage announced that one of the largest private residential landholdings in South Mississauga has gone on sale for the first time in its history. 5 acres and features some decidedly unique amenities–including an underground pedestrian tunnel. , was custom-designed by David Small Designs and built in 2005 on what was originally a vacant parcel. “While contemporary builds often prioritize minimalism, 530 Indian Road offers a distinct counterpoint in classical European architecture,” Ciro Napolitano, the listing’s sales representative with Sam McDadi Real Estate Brokerage, said in a statement. “The original owners built this home on a rare double-deep parcel in 2005 and poured artisanal detail into every square inch. From the double security gates to the underground tunnel leading to the pool house, it genuinely feels like Lorne Park’s private Casa Loma. ” According to the brokerage, which announced a record-breaking, multi-million-dollar home sale last month, the expansive property boasts an irregular 115-by-613-foot lot depth, which is not typically found in the upscale neighbourhood’s established grid. The eight-bedroom (three below grade), 11-washroom property’s Casa Loma comparison comes from its traditional European castle proportions, which includes Indiana-style cut stone, hand-carved classical columns, a multi-tiered front motor court fountain. The interior includes coffered ceilings, crown moulding, marble flooring, five natural gas fireplaces and a curved staircase. The house contains dual commercial kitchens, one with a walk-in refrigeration room. On the lower level, buyers will have access to an entertainment wing with a walk-in wine cellar, billiards hall, fitness centre, games lounge and guest quarters.

items.title: Third Suspect Named as Police Reveal Mississauga Arson Attacks Targeted Someone She Knew
items.summary: Peel Regional Police have named Madison Varga, 30, as the third suspect being sought in connection with two deliberately set fires at a Clarkson apartment building near Lakeshore Road West and Southdown Road. According to acting Det. Sgt. Natosha McBride, one of the two people already arrested in the case had a prior relationship with a resident of the building targeted in both fires. Police say the blazes were set in a third-floor hallway on Sept. 20 and again early the next morning, and investigators believe the same unit was deliberately targeted each time. Const. Laurie McCann told reporters at a Thursday news conference that one officer who responded to the scene suffered a hand injury that required surgery. No residents were seriously hurt, though 18 occupants of the seven-storey building were taken to hospital for smoke inhalation, and the second fire forced a large-scale evacuation that displaced several residents. Police estimate the two fires caused about $1 million in damage. Joshua Pedersen, 28, and Morgan Murphy, 27, both face arson-related charges, while Varga remains at large.

items.title: Living Arts Centre to Host Nov. 13 Job and Settlement Fair for New Canadians
items.summary: The Canadian Immigrant Fair returns to Mississauga's Living Arts Centre on Nov. 13, offering free workshops, career advice and giveaways for newcomers to Canada. According to organizers, the event brings together employers, recruiters, educational institutions and immigrant-serving organizations under one roof at the Living Arts Dr. venue. Organizers say the fair gives newcomers a one-stop opportunity to explore career options, learn about education and immigration pathways and connect directly with service providers. Attendees can also get practical advice on building a future in Canada, organizers added. The fair is aimed specifically at helping recent arrivals navigate the job market and settlement process in the Mississauga area.

items.title: Explore Mississauga like a city planner on World Urbanism Day
items.summary: Discover the City’s many tools and resources that can help you understand how urban planning shapes your favourite streets, parks and community spaces. Have you ever wondered why some streets are bustling with activity while others are quiet and peaceful? Or how it’s decided where parks and public art are located? The answer is urban planning. World Urbanism Day is on November 8, and residents are invited to discover their inner city planner and learn more about the work that goes into building a city like Mississauga. Urban planning is about more than what gets built and where, it’s about creating places that are functional, attractive and connected. Professional planners think about how people move around a city; the connections between roads, walkways and green spaces and how neighbourhoods evolve over time as the city grows. Behind every street, waterfront trail and local park are thousands of planning decisions that have helped shape the city. Whether you’re curious about developments in your neighbourhood or wondering how planning decisions are made, the City has many different ways to help you start thinking like a planner and explore how cities take shape. The Mississauga Civic Centre is open to the public and home to the Downtown Model, a miniature replica of our city’s downtown core. It shows how planners might visualize the ways that landmarks, buildings, streets and parks connect with one another. Explore the model and see if you can spot Kariya Park, Square One and other major landmarks. Then on November 19, you can join us for an urban design open house. Meet city planning staff and learn about the City’s ongoing urban design program review, which influences the look and feel of our community.

items.title: Peel Police Charge Two, Still Searching for Third Suspect in Clarkson Apartment Arson Case
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say two people have been charged and a third suspect is wanted after two deliberately set fires at a Clarkson apartment building near Lakeshore Road West and Southdown Road caused an estimated $1 million in damage. According to police, the fires were set in a third-floor hallway on Sunday, Sept. 20, and Monday, Sept. 21, and investigators believe occupants of one unit were deliberately targeted both times. Police said no significant injuries were reported, though the second fire triggered a large-scale evacuation that displaced several residents, and 18 people were taken to hospital for smoke inhalation. Police said they identified three people believed to be involved in the incidents. Joshua Pedersen, 28, of no fixed address, was arrested in Hamilton on Oct. 15 and charged with two counts of arson disregarding human life, two counts of mischief over $5,000, break and enter with intent to commit an indictable offence, and possession of break-in instruments. Morgan Murphy, 27, of Burlington, was arrested on Oct. 26 and charged with two counts each of conspiracy to commit an indictable offence and arson disregarding human life. Both were held in custody pending bail hearings.

items.title: City Removes Fake QR Code Stickers Found on Mississauga Parking Machines
items.summary: The City of Mississauga says it became aware on Nov. 4 of fraudulent QR code stickers placed on Pay and Display parking machines across the city. According to the city, staff were deployed immediately and removed the stickers, which were designed to redirect users to third-party payment sites not affiliated with the city. The city said scanning and using those codes put residents' personal and financial information at risk. Officials said QR code stickers are never used to collect payment for parking in Mississauga, and that the only legitimate way to pay is through a parking machine's digital payment prompts, which accept coins, payment apps such as Apple Pay or Google Wallet, and major credit cards, with PayByPhone also available in Streetsville. The city said it continues to monitor parking machines and equipment and will respond quickly to any further reports of fraudulent codes.
